newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's PRI falls short of majority in lower house.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's PRI falls short of majority in lower house.

text.p: Mexico's long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) won 164 of the 300 directly elected seats in the lower house of Congress but still fell short of an outright majority, the final official count showed on Friday.

Under Mexico's complex electoral law the PRI needed at least 167 of the directly elected seats in the 500-seat chamber and 42.2 percent of the national vote to again clinch the absolute majority it has enjoyed for the past 68 years.
"The PRI did not receive an absolute majority in this election," said Juan Molinar, a citizen councilor on the Federal Electoral Institute (IFE).

The results, still subject to appeal, gave the left-wing opposition Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) 70 deputies, followed closely by the conservative National Action Party (PAN) with 65. The PT workers party won one seat, the results from the IFE said.
Another 200 seats have yet to be allocated in the Chamber of Deputies under a system of proportional representation. That process is expected to be completed by Aug. 23.
Sunday's watershed mid-term elections gave opposition parties unprecedented gains and shocked the PRI by stripping it of its absolute hold on power.
The new multi-party chamber, which in the past has simply been a rubber stamp for legislation proposed by the president, will meet for the first time in September.
Mexico's powerful Interior Minister Emilio Chuayffet on Friday praised the results of the vote, saying that elections were the only way to transform Mexican society.

"The results were encouraging for everyone. They expressed a clear and pluralistic mandate and our Congress will be a place of reflection, the defence of ideas and convictions," Chuayfett said in a speech.
In Sunday's election, the PRD candidate Cuauhtemoc Cardenas won the race for Mexico City mayor in the first vote for a mayor in Mexico's largest city in decades.
Six state governorships were also up for grabs, with results showing the PRI probably retaining the governor's post in four states and the PAN likely winning two states.
